title: ToolPRO Automotive Tool Kit 201 Piece $105 (C&C Only) @ Supercheap Auto
body:
Deal: ToolPRO Automotive Tool Kit 201 Piece $105 (C&C Only) @ Supercheap Auto

[stratbargain] @xdave I still use the socket set my parents got me when I got my L's and I'm 45. A great present idea :)
[xdave] I have some decent SCA and Repco MechPro tool kits already myself but can't help but feel a little jealous of the tools that he will get to use haha :D
[17833] Thanks OP. Had $5 credit and bought a $100 gift card from this offer https://www.ozbargain.com.au/node/973954 to get $10 cashback, effectively paid $90.
[sumyungguy] … but the 68 imperial/SAE items are somewhat useless.
[Springfield] Exactly. Total dead weight for the average Aussie garage. They clutter the case and make it a pain to navigate the metric sockets you actually need. Manufacturers love doing it just to artificially pump up the 'piece count' on the box.
Guaranteed the 10mm metric socket will vanish into a black hole on day one, while all 68 pristine imperial pieces stay exactly where they are for the next 20 years.
[Pusdi] A telescopic magnet is a lifesaver to retrieve dropped parts/tools in the engine bay. Probably need a matching telescopic mirror for some of the black holes though
[Jimothy Wongingtons] At least it’s all tools in this kit not like 30 blades for Stanley knife and 69 of the shittest non uv rated 100mm zip ties
[tunzafun001] I have the all metric version of this…with 3 x 10mm sockets (now 2).
Only down side was I broke a 3/8 ratchet. They replaced it, but the new ratchet shape is different and it doesn't fit in the kit.
[birdbath] imperial is useful for lawn mowers or other power equipment. many of the large manufacturers are American like briggs and stratton, john deere, MTD, ect.
plus older aussie stuff too
[Springfield] Funnily enough, my 15yo Masport with a Briggs engine is all metric too, right down to the blade bolts. The imperial pieces truly are cursed to stay pristine forever.
[JinXR] Not for my American made zero turn mower - it's all imperial.
[CheapCookie] If I could do it all over again, I wouldn't have brought my gear wrench starter tool trolley set up.
I have a load of spanners collecting dust in the imperial/SAE size now….
[Edog] Hey Guys, in the market for a solid mid-tier socket setup, but every all-in-one "150-piece" cases are complete garbage with useless bloat screwdriver bits, SAE/Imperial sizes and 12-point sockets that round off sump plugs.
I'd rather buy 2 or 3 separate blow-mould cases to cover 1/4", 3/8", and 1/2" drives.
Requirements:
Pure Metric (Zero SAE - which unfortunately kills Gearwrench).
100% 6-Point sockets (both shallow & deep).
Decent Cr-V steel with solid 72+ tooth ratchets.
Must come in proper latching cases, not foam trays.
What exact sets/part numbers are best value right now for this? Bahco, Kincrome, or similar. Appreciate any deal links!
[birdbath] I really like koken stuff from japan. Excellent quality with nice and grippy knurling.
This 3/8” set on amazon seems like a good price ($209):
https://www.amazon.com.au/Ko-ken-3286Z-socket-wrench-assembl…
[Edog] Thanks bro, Koken is absolute top-tier gear and $209 for that 3286Z set on Amazon Japan is an unreal deal.
The main hurdle for me is the lack of deep sockets in that tin, I need deep 6-points for recessed bolts and studs.
I checked the matching Ko-ken Z-EAL deep rail (RS3300MZ/8), but it’s sitting around $200 AUD. Paying $200 for 8 deep sockets when the entire 21-piece master kit is $209 hurts physically.
What’s the smartest way to solve this deep-socket gap without blowing $400+ total just for the 3/8'' drive?
[revheadgl] Above mid tier, but all the tools you asked for and super nice too. Not stupidly expensive either in my opinion.
I can't link directly to any stores anyway as it will be deleted as spam, but definitely worth shopping around. Eg; TKD deal https://www.ozbargain.com.au/node/973957
$111 Milwaukee 48229504 28pce 1/4" Drive Ratchet & Socket (Metric) Set
https://www.milwaukeetool.com.au/hand-tools/sockets-and-wren…
$189 Milwaukee MRSS36 32pce 3/8" Drive Metric Ratchet and Socket Set with BONUS Spark Plug Sockets https://www.milwaukeetool.com.au/hand-tools/sockets-and-wren…
$277 Milwaukee 48229510 28pce 1/2" Drive Metric Socket Ratchet Set
https://www.milwaukeetool.com.au/hand-tools/sockets-and-wren…
[Edog] Legend mate, thanks for pointing out the Milwaukee lineup!
That Milwaukee 3/8" set for $189 at Sydney Tools looks like the winner for 3/8". Ticks every single box: 6-point metric, zero SAE bloat, standard + deep sockets included, 90-tooth ratchet, and flat anti-roll sides in a hard case.
The Ko-ken Z-EAL option looked tempting, but getting 8 deep sockets imported on a rail costs $200 on its own, which completely ruins the value proposition.
Currently looking at building a multi-drive setup by mixing brands:
1/4" Drive: Milwaukee 48229504, $111
3/8" Drive: Milwaukee MRSS36, $189
1/2" Drive: Bahco 6-Point Metric Set ($130–$160), Heavy-duty 6-point for higher torque jobs.
A couple of quick questions:
Is there any practical downside to running Bahco for 1/2" alongside Milwaukee for 1/4" and 3/8"?
Is it smarter to keep all three 1/4'',3/8'' and 1/2'' under Milwaukee to push total spend over $499 and trigger the Sydney Tools bonus contractor bag?
Do these Milwaukee hand tool sets ever drop lower during Father's Day promos, or is $189 pretty much the bottom floor?
Appreciate the insights, champion!
[revheadgl] Happy my comments were useful to you:)
Absolutely no reason you can't mix and match, but you might not like the Bahco after using the Milwaukee.
There are occasional deals. Tool Kit Depot regularly have 10 percent off and Power Tools Specialists have had 20 per cent off twice within the last year.
TKD have 10 off til midnight tonight but they only stock the 3/8 and 1/2 kit.
You could take a punt on the chance of a deal on BF, but there is an equal chance of no deals, lol.
We had that Milwaukee tool bag for work and it was a good thing. Very well made & tough. My brother is still using it, If you didn't want it, should be pretty easy to sell for $70-80.
So just my final thoughts, I really like Milwaukee hand tools & accessories and I have fair collection. I only have the 1 socket set so far and it's a joy to use. So well made. As is everything else I have from them.
[Edog] @revheadgl: Appreciate the follow-up mate! That’s absolute gold info on the $80 resale value for the bag, that’s not bad at all.
In the end, the math forced my hand to split the drives and snag some bargains online:
3/8" Locked in the Ko-ken Z-EAL 3286Z set via Amazon. It's the Porsche of tools, made in Japan, ultra-compact profiles, and sick reviews that were too good to pass up. I’ll pair it with a separate deep rail to cover the gap.
1/4" Going Milwaukee at $111. For 1/4" dash and engine bay work, having standard + deep in that compact hard case is an absolute no-brainer.
1/2" Ended up pulling the trigger on the Milwaukee 1/2" set for $229 free shipping on eBay (Depot Australia). Beats the $277 retail price by almost $50 cash upfront.
Really appreciate you taking the time to share your experience with the lineup, proper legend!
[sumyungguy] My long time base kit is Bahco 34-piece but I also rate Wera Zyklop Speed Ratchet which keeps me trawling for pre-owned Wera stuff. Linked here a few years ago for $66
[tunzafun001] Can't get this still anywhere?
I grabbed one in 2018.
All metric, 6 point sockets, 72 tooth ratchets.
I broke one. But they replaced it no questions.
https://www.ozbargain.com.au/node/535098
[Ciumumma] Op, you would be better to buy your Son roadside assist rather than a toolkit, which is fairly useless on any modern vehicle.
